headline: Rent growth offsets softer occupancy as buybacks trim equity
summary_short: Revenue rose 2.8% y/y to $470.1M on higher rental rates, diluted EPS grew to $0.31 from $0.28, and Adjusted FFO grew 5.4% y/y to $186.0M even as portfolio occupancy eased to 95.6% and turnover ticked up.
summary_long: Revenue grew 2.8% y/y to $470.1M on higher rental rates (Same-Home rent +2.6% to $2,346), partly offset by softer Same-Home occupancy (96.0% vs 96.4%) and higher turnover (8.1% vs 7.5%). Net income (common) rose 7.6% to $113.6M as revenue growth outpaced expenses and property-sale gains increased. FFO/Core FFO/AFFO all grew y/y ($194.0M/$202.8M/$186.0M). AMH repurchased $123.0M of stock and paid a $0.33/share dividend, up 10% y/y. Long-term debt was flat y/y at $5,130.1M (no new notes issued, vs $646M in Q2 2025); equity fell 5.0% to $6,807.6M on buybacks. Cash fell to $83.7M from $323.3M y/y on last year's note proceeds and this year's repurchases. No forward guidance disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Net income grew as rents and other single-family property revenues outpaced total expense growth, with higher net gains on property sales, partially offset by lower other income.
Revenue growth was primarily driven by higher rental rates.
Reflects net income growth combined with a ~2.8% y/y decline in weighted diluted shares (371.1M to 360.8M) from buybacks.
Same drivers as diluted EPS: net income growth plus a lower weighted average share count from repurchases.
Increases in rents and other single-family property revenues exceeded increases in total expenses, plus higher net gains on property sales, partially offset by lower other income and expense, net.
Not separately explained in the release; mirrors net income growth plus the standard NAREIT real-estate D&A add-back.
Not separately explained in the release; FFO growth plus modestly higher one-time addback items (transaction costs, share-based comp) versus the prior year.
Core FFO growth plus lower Recurring Capital Expenditures ($15.9M vs $20.5M y/y) and lower leasing costs, per the company's own AFFO reconciliation.
Y/y decline reflects 2025's one-time $646.4M unsecured senior notes issuance and this year's $238.2M of share repurchases, per the financing-activities discussion.
Roughly unchanged y/y: no new senior notes were issued in 2026 (vs $646.4M issued in 2025), offset by a higher revolving-credit-facility balance.
Decline is consistent with $238.2M of share repurchases during the year exceeding retained net income; not explicitly framed as an equity driver in the release.
